title: A protocol for wide-scope non-target analysis of contaminants in small amounts of biota using bead beating tissuelyser extraction and LC-HRMS
author: Gil-Solsona, Rodriguez-Mozaz, et al.
materials: Samples were analysed in a Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass analyser (Thermo Scientific) in Data Dependent acquisition (DDA), acquiring MS/MS for the 5 most intense ions and Data Independent (DIA) analysis at 35 eV of collision energy in both cases for MS/MS and high energy functions.

steps.title: Prepare zirconium beads
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g of zirconium beads and add them to the extraction tube.

steps.title: Clean mortar and homogenize sample
steps.instruction: Clean a ceramic mortar with Milli‑Q water, ethanol and dry it; then homogenize the samples in the mortar.

steps.title: Weigh sample into extraction tube
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.1 g of dried krill or fish matrix and place it into the extraction tube containing the beads.

steps.title: Add surrogate standards and evaporate
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of a 1 µg·mL⁻¹ surrogate‑standard solution (mixture of Clothianidine‑d₃, Caffeine‑d₃ and Benzotriazole‑d₄ in acetone) to the tube and allow the solvent to evaporate for 30–60 min.

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the citrate‑acetonitrile extraction mixture as follows:

substeps.instruction: Weigh 19.213 g citric acid (S1) and dissolve in 1000 mL HPLC‑grade water.
Weigh 14.705 g trisodium citrate di‑hydrate (S2) and dissolve in 1000 mL HPLC‑grade water.
Mix 118 mL of S1 with 82 mL of S2.
Add 200 mL of the S1:S2 (59:41) mixture to 200 mL acetonitrile; this solution is the extraction mixture.

steps.title: Add extraction mixture to sample
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the citrate‑buffer/acetonitrile extraction mixture to the tube.

steps.title: Perform bead beating extraction
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a tissuelyser (or Cryolys) and run for 30 s at power 5.5 to homogenize the sample.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 11 000 rcf for 10 min and transfer the supernatant into a clean glass tube.

steps.title: Repeat extraction two more times
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 4–7 two additional times, adding the supernatant each time to the same glass tube (total three extractions).

steps.title: Reduce extract volume by N₂ evaporation
steps.instruction: Use a nitrogen evaporator to reduce the combined extract volume to approximately 50 % (≈1.5 mL) to remove excess organic solvent.

steps.title: Dilute extract in buffered water
steps.instruction: Transfer the reduced extract to a glass bottle containing 100 mL HPLC‑grade water adjusted to pH 6.5 with ammonia and formic acid.

steps.title: Rinse extraction glassware
steps.instruction: Rinse the glass tubes three times with 3 mL HPLC‑grade water each time.

steps.title: Condition mixed‑mode SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Condition each homemade mixed‑mode SPE cartridge (containing 0.2 g Sepra ZT, 0.1 g Sepra ZTL‑WCX, 0.1 g Sepra ZTL‑WAX and 0.15 g Isolute ENV+) sequentially with HPLC‑grade methanol then HPLC‑grade water under gravity flow.

steps.title: Load extract onto SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Load the diluted extract onto the conditioned cartridge at approximately 1 drop per second.

steps.title: Dry cartridge with air
steps.instruction: Pass air through the cartridge for 3 min to dry it.

steps.title: Elute with Mixture A and dry
steps.instruction: Elute the cartridge with 4 mL of Mixture A, then circulate air for 2 min.

substeps.instruction: Mixture A is prepared by mixing 470 mL methanol, 470 mL ethyl acetate and 60 mL 32 % ammonia solution (final ammonia concentration 2 %).

steps.title: Elute with Mixture B and dry
steps.instruction: Elute the cartridge with 2 mL of Mixture B, then circulate air for 2 min.

substeps.instruction: Mixture B is prepared by mixing 490 mL methanol, 490 mL ethyl acetate and 20 mL formic acid (88–90 %, final concentration 1.8 %).

steps.title: Concentrate eluate to minimal volume
steps.instruction: Reduce the combined eluates in the glass tube to the minimum volume using a gentle nitrogen stream.

steps.title: Transfer to HPLC vials (first aliquot)
steps.instruction: Transfer the concentrated extract from the glass tube to an HPLC vial.

steps.title: Add methanol, vortex, transfer (repeat 3×)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL methanol to the glass tube, vortex for 15 s, and transfer the methanol extract to the HPLC vial; repeat this washing step three times to ensure complete recovery.

steps.title: Dry vial extracts under N₂
steps.instruction: Dry the combined extracts in the HPLC vial with a gentle nitrogen stream.

steps.title: Reconstitute with methanol and water
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the dried residue with 0.5 mL HPLC‑grade methanol, then add 0.5 mL HPLC‑grade water.

steps.title: Inject sample into UPLC‑HRMS
steps.instruction: Inject 10 µL of the final extract directly into the UPLC‑HRMS system (no filtration).

steps.title: Set LC conditions for positive mode
steps.instruction: Configure the LC for positive ionisation: Acquity UPLC C18 column (100 Å, 1.8 µm, 2.1 × 100 mm), column temperature 40 °C, mobile phase A 0.1 % formic acid in methanol, mobile phase B 0.1 % formic acid in water; gradient: 5 % A initial, 75 % A at 7 min, 100 % A at 10 min, hold to 15 min, return to 5 % A at 17 min, hold to 23 min; sample volume 10 µL.

steps.title: Set LC conditions for negative mode
steps.instruction: Configure the LC for negative ionisation: same column and temperature, mobile phase A 5 mM ammonium acetate in methanol, mobile phase B 5 mM ammonium acetate in water; gradient: 5 % A initial, 50 % A at 3 min, 90 % A at 6 min, 100 % A at 13 min, hold to 17 min, 5 % A at 18 min, hold to 20 min; sample volume 10 µL.

steps.title: Configure HRMS parameters
steps.instruction: Set HRMS source parameters (both positive and negative modes): spray voltage 3000 V (+) / 2800 V (‑), capillary temperature 350 °C, sheath gas 40, auxiliary gas 10, max spray current 100, probe heater temperature 350 °C, S‑Lens RF level 60.

steps.title: Acquire DDA and DIA data
steps.instruction: Run the Q‑Exactive Orbitrap in Data‑Dependent Acquisition (DDA) acquiring MS/MS for the 5 most intense ions, and in Data‑Independent Acquisition (DIA) at 35 eV collision energy for MS/MS and high‑energy functions.
